<reason>Elite, genuinely close debate. B built a clean case (debt exists, money exists, only courts connect them) and delivered the single best speech — its closing convergence attack that CON also uses the assets with "no threshold at all." But A left more damaging material standing at the end: the multi-jurisdiction creditor queue that no single statute can solve, and the exposure that B's "manifest + overwhelming collective judgment" trigger is a diplomatic headcount that spares the strong — neither answered after A's second rebuttal. A's closing directly engaged B's convergence attack with the reversibility distinction (a freeze can be unwound; extinguished title cannot) and crystallized the "confiscation runs downhill" frame. B's closing, for all its force, ignored A's two heaviest live points. A's two clipped turns are real execution costs that keep this from being a larger margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's second rebuttal sequence: showing the queue survives B's authorizing statute (statutes can't bind foreign forums or rival creditors), then dismantling B's aggression gate as "a headcount, not a legal test" that great powers can always block — B never answered either point. B's closing counter-thrust (CON's mechanism also uses the assets with no finding at all) was the strongest reply but only partially blunted by A's reversibility answer.</best_rebuttal>
